header.what: One run of Klaxon's diagnosis agent on the case poison-message: claude-opus-5-5 through Claude Code on Aravind's seat (live). Its tools read incident data captured from Klaxon's live stack.

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer is blocked by a poison message, provider-events/0@229 (evt_000681, pay_000619), whose amount is invalid ('amount must be positive integer cents'). It was recreated at 07:56:08 with BAD_EVENTS=retry, so it retries that message indefinitely, every 15 s and at attempt 13+, instead of setting it aside. Every later message queues behind it, so ledger lag grows (176, then 222), the money check cannot settle, and BooksBehindProvider fires. payment-confirmer has BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter. It dead-lettered the same message and moved on, so its lag is 0. evt_000681 was a second webhook for pay_000619. The first, evt_000680 at offset 228 for 1260 cents, was booked and confirmed. Open: evt_000681's type and real amount, whether the provider truly sent a bad amount, and BAD_EVENTS's value before the 07:56:08 deploy.

evidence.shows: The money check could not run: 222 ledger messages are not yet handled and payment-confirmer has 0. This confirms the alert and shows the backlog growing.
ledger-consumer keeps failing on provider-events/0@229 with 'amount must be positive integer cents' and retries the same message. Backoff has reached 15 s and attempts have reached 13.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 07:56:08 with LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and BAD_EVENTS=retry. payment-confirmer has BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter. No other service changed since 07:52.
At 07:56:13, payment-confirmer dead-lettered the same message for the same reason and moved on. ledger-consumer's endless retries started at that same moment.
Offset 229 is evt_000681, keyed pay_000619. webhook-receiver accepted it at 07:56:13 with HTTP 200.
pay_000619 already had a valid payment.succeeded event, evt_000680, for 1260 cents, which was posted and confirmed. evt_000681 is a later, malformed event for the same payment.

proposed_fix.summary: Set BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter on ledger-consumer, matching payment-confirmer, or roll back to its settings from before 07:56:08. Restart it so it dead-letters offset 229 and drains the backlog. Then inspect evt_000681 in the dead-letter queue, check its true type and amount against the provider's records, and repair or replay it once validated. Rerun the money check to confirm it settles.

diagnosis.blast_radius: This affects only how ledger-consumer handles events it cannot book: malformed events go to the dead-letter queue instead of blocking the stream. Until someone reviews it, evt_000681 stays out of the ledger, so the ledger may differ from the provider for pay_000619. Other events that fail validation would also be dead-lettered quietly, so the dead-letter queue needs monitoring and an alert.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with BAD_EVENTS=retry, its current setting. The idempotent ledger handler prevents double booking. Dead-lettered messages can be replayed from the dead-letter queue.
